simple.meaning: עֲרָד (ʻărâd) is a Hebrew word meaning “an onager.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲרָד (H6167) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֲרָד (H6167) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֲרָד (ʻărâd) / H6167 is traced through Daniel 5:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He was driven from the sons of men, and his heart was made like the animals’, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. He was fed with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky; until he knew that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and that he sets up over it whomever he will.
